appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise, voyant Albertine entrer... mettre partout le désordre, me ruiner, me causer tant de chagrins, me disait : « si Monsieur à la place de cette fille qui lui fait perdre tout son temps avait pris un petit secrétaire bien élevé qui aurait classé toutes les paperoles de Monsieur ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise's quoted remark casts Albertine as disruptive, costly, and a waste of the narrator's time, unfavorably contrasted with an imagined well-behaved secretary.

appraisal_events.evidence: En me faisant perdre mon temps, en me faisant du chagrin, Albertine m'avait peut-être été plus utile, même au point de vue littéraire, qu'un secrétaire qui eût rangé mes paperoles.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly reverses Françoise's practical judgment, crediting the suffering and disorder Albertine caused with being more valuable to his literary work than an orderly secretary would have been.

status_effects.explanation: Françoise's domestic complaint frames Albertine as disorderly and costly, a mildly diminishing practical judgment.

The narrator's retrospective reappraisal elevates Albertine's worth by crediting her disruptive presence with artistic value exceeding that of an efficient secretary, though the claim is hedged with 'peut-être.'

ambiguities: The narrator initially says he found Françoise's judgment of Albertine wise, then explicitly says he was 'perhaps wrong' to think so, reversing the evaluative direction within the same passage; the hedge 'peut-être' in the reversal itself tempers how strongly the elevation should be read.
